row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_FWDNUMRINGS = 0x00000001 Specifies whether the number of rings for a no-answer can be specified when forwarding calls on no answer. If TRUE, the valid range is provided in the dwMinFwdNumRings and dwMaxFwdNumRings members of the LINEADDRESSCAPS structure.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_FWDSTATUSVALID
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_FWDSTATUSVALID = 0x00020000 Specifies whether the forwarding status in the LINEADDRESSSTATUS structure for this address is valid or is at most a "best estimate," given absence of accurate confirmation by the switch or network.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_HOLDMAKESNEW
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_HOLDMAKESNEW = 0x04000000 When a call on this address is placed on hold, using lineHold or external action, a new call is automatically created, most likely in LINECALLSTATE_DIALTONE. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_NOEXTERNALCALLS
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_NOEXTERNALCALLS = 0x10000000 The address is associated with an internal line on a PBX that is restricted in such a way that it cannot be used to place calls to an address outside the switch, for example, if it is an intercom. The application can use this indication to assist the user in selecting the correct call appearance to use for making a call. When this bit is off, it does not necessarily indicate that the address can be used to make external calls, because the service provider may not be cognizant of the line type. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_NOINTERNALCALLS
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_NOINTERNALCALLS = 0x08000000 The address is associated with a direct CO line (trunk), and cannot be used to make internal calls on a PBX. The application can use this indication to assist the user in selecting the correct call appearance to use for making a call. When this bit is off, it does not necessarily indicate that the address can be used to make internal calls, because the service provider may not be cognizant of the line type. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_ORIGOFFHOOK
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_ORIGOFFHOOK = 0x000000040 Specifies whether the originating party's phone can automatically be taken offhook when making calls.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PARTIALDIAL
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PARTIALDIAL = 0x0001000 Specifies whether partial dialing is available.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PICKUPCALLWAIT
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PICKUPCALLWAIT = 0x0040000 TRUE if linePickup can be used to pick up a call detected by the user as a call-waiting call otherwise, FALSE.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PICKUPGROUPID
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PICKUPGROUPID = 0x00000002 Specifies whether a group identifier is required for call pickup.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PREDICTIVEDIALER
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PREDICTIVEDIALER = 0x0080000 This address has enhanced call progress monitoring capabilities which can be applied to outgoing calls to determine call states such as ringback, busy, specialinfo, and connected, or the media type of the device answering the call. It may also have the ability to automatically transfer outgoing calls to another address when a call reaches any of a predefined set of states. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_QUEUE
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_QUEUE = 0x0100000 This address is not associated with a particular station or physical device, but is a holding place where calls wait for further processing. The calls placed in the queue may receive a particular treatment. They may also be automatically transferred when a particular resource becomes available. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_ROUTEPOINT
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_ROUTEPOINT = 0x0200000 This address is not associated with a particular station or physical device, but is a holding place where calls wait for routing by the application. The application examines the called address, and can redirect the call to another address. The call can also be automatically transferred if a routing timeout expires The switch usually assumes a default routing. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_SECURE
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_SECURE = 0x00000004 Specifies whether calls on this address can be made secure at call-setup time.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_SETCALLINGID
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_SETCALLINGID = 0x2000000 The application can choose to set the CallingPartyID member in LINECALLPARAMS when calling lineMakeCall and other functions that accept a LINECALLPARAMS structure. The service provider will, if the content of the identifier is acceptable and a path is available, pass the identifier along to the called party to indicate the identity of the calling party. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_SETUPCONFNULL
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_SETUPCONFNULL = 0x00000200 Specifies whether setting up a conference call starts out with an initial call (FALSE) or with no initial call (TRUE).

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_TRANSFERHELD
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_TRANSFERHELD = 0x00001000 Specifies whether a hard-held call can be transferred. Often, only calls on consultation hold can be transferred.

name: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_TRANSFERMAKE
title: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_TRANSFERMAKE = 0x00002000 Specifies whether an entirely new call can be established for use as a consultation call on transfer.

name: LINEADDRESSMODE_ADDRESSID
title: LINEADDRESSMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSMODE_ADDRESSID = 0x00000001 The address is specified with a small integer in the range zero (0) to dwNumAddresses minus one (-1), where the dwNumAddresses member is the value in the line's device capabilities, which is specified in the LINEDEVCAPS structure.

name: LINEADDRESSMODE_DIALABLEADDR
title: LINEADDRESSMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSMODE_DIALABLEADDR = 0x00000002 The address is specified through its phone number.

name: LINEADDRESSSHARING_BRIDGEDEXCL
title: LINEADDRESSSHARING (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSHARING_BRIDGEDEXCL = 0x00000002 The address is bridged to one or more other stations. The first line to activate a call on the line will have exclusive access to the address and calls that may exist on it. Other lines will not be able to use the bridged address while it is in use.

name: LINEADDRESSSHARING_BRIDGEDNEW
title: LINEADDRESSSHARING (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSHARING_BRIDGEDNEW = 0x00000004 The address is bridged with one or more other stations. The first line to activate a call on the line will have exclusive access to only the corresponding call. Other applications that use the address will result in new and separate call appearances.

name: LINEADDRESSSHARING_BRIDGEDSHARED
title: LINEADDRESSSHARING (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSHARING_BRIDGEDSHARED = 0x00000008 The address is bridged with one or more other lines. All bridged parties can share in calls on the address, which then functions as a conference.

name: LINEADDRESSSHARING_MONITORED
title: LINEADDRESSSHARING (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSHARING_MONITORED= 0x00000010 This is an address whose idle/busy status is made available to this line.

name: LINEADDRESSSHARING_PRIVATE
title: LINEADDRESSSHARING (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSHARING_PRIVATE = 0x00000001 The address is private to the user's line. It is not assigned to any other station.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_CAPSCHANGE
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_CAPSCHANGE = 0x00000100 Indicates that, due to configuration changes made by the user or other circumstances, one or more of the members in the LINEADDRESSCAPS structure for the address have changed. The application should use the lineGetAddressCaps function to read the updated structure. If a service provider sends a LINE_ADDRESSSTATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later; applications negotiating a previous API version will receive LINE_LINEDEVSTATE messages specifying LINEDEVSTATE_REINIT, requiring them to shut down and reinitialize their connection to TAPI to obtain the updated information.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_DEVSPECIFIC
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_DEVSPECIFIC = 0x00000002 The device-specific item of the address status has changed.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_FORWARD
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_FORWARD = 0x00000040 The forwarding status of the address has changed, including possibly the number of rings for determining a no-answer condition. The application should check the address status to determine details about the address's current forwarding status.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_INUSEMANY
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_INUSEMANY = 0x00000010 The monitored or bridged address has changed from being in use by one station to being in use by more than one station.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_INUSEONE
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_INUSEONE = 0x00000008 The address has changed from idle or in use by many bridged stations to being in use by just one station.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_INUSEZERO
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_INUSEZERO = 0x00000004 The address has changed to idle. It is not in use by any stations.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_NUMCALLS
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_NUMCALLS = 0x00000020 The number of calls on the address has changed. This is the result of events such as a new incoming call, an outgoing call on the address, or a call changing its hold status. This flag covers changes in any of the members dwNumActiveCalls, dwNumOnHoldCalls and dwNumOnHoldPendingCalls in the LINEADDRESSSTATUS. The application should check all three of these members when it receives a LINE_ADDRESSSTATE (numCalls) message.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_OTHER
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_OTHER = 0x00000001 Address-status items other than those listed below have changed. The application should check the current address status to determine which items have changed.

name: LINEADDRESSSTATE_TERMINALS
title: LINEADDRESSSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSSTATE_TERMINALS = 0x00000080 The terminal settings for the address have changed.

name: LINEADDRESSTYPE_DOMAINNAME
title: LINEADDRESSTYPE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSTYPE_DOMAINNAME = 0x00000008 Address type is a domain name.

name: LINEADDRESSTYPE_EMAILNAME
title: LINEADDRESSTYPE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSTYPE_EMAILNAME = 0x00000004 Address type is an e-mail name.

name: LINEADDRESSTYPE_IPADDRESS
title: LINEADDRESSTYPE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSTYPE_IPADDRESS = 0x00000010 Address type is an IP address.

name: LINEADDRESSTYPE_PHONENUMBER
title: LINEADDRESSTYPE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSTYPE_PHONENUMBER = 0x00000001 Address type is a standard phone number.

name: LINEADDRESSTYPE_SDP
title: LINEADDRESSTYPE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEADDRESSTYPE_SDP = 0x00000002 Address type is Session Description Protocol (SDP) conference.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_ALTSPEECHDATA
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_ALTSPEECHDATA = 0x00000010 The alternate transfer of speech or unrestricted data on the same call (ISDN).

name: LINEBEARERMODE_DATA
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_DATA = 0x00000008 The unrestricted data transfer on the call. The data rate is specified separately.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_MULTIUSE
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_MULTIUSE = 0x00000004 The multiuse mode defined by ISDN.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_NONCALLSIGNALING
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_NONCALLSIGNALING = 0x00000020 This corresponds to a non-call-associated signaling connection from the application to the service provider or switch. This is treated as a media stream by TAPI.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_PASSTHROUGH
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_PASSTHROUGH = 0x00000040 When a call is active in LINEBEARERMODE_PASSTHROUGH, the service provider gives direct access to the attached hardware for control by the application. This mode is used primarily by applications desiring temporary direct control over asynchronous modems, accessed through the Win32 communication functions, for the purpose of configuring or using special features not otherwise supported by the service provider. TAPI version 1.4 and later.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_RESTRICTEDDATA
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_RESTRICTEDDATA = 0x00000080 Bearer service for digital data in which only the low-order seven bits of each octet may contain user data (for example, for Switched 56kbit/s service). TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_SPEECH
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_SPEECH = 0x00000002 This corresponds to G.711 speech transmission on the call. The network can use processing techniques such as analog transmission, echo cancellation, and compression/decompression. Bit integrity is not assured. Speech is not intended to support fax and modem media types.

name: LINEBEARERMODE_VOICE
title: LINEBEARERMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBEARERMODE_VOICE = 0x00000001 This is a regular 3.1 kHz analog voice-grade bearer service. Bit integrity is not assured. Voice can support fax and modem media types.

name: LINEBUSYMODE_STATION
title: LINEBUSYMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBUSYMODE_STATION = 0x00000001 The busy signal indicates that the called party's station is busy. This is usually signaled with a normal busy tone.

name: LINEBUSYMODE_TRUNK
title: LINEBUSYMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBUSYMODE_TRUNK = 0x00000002 The busy signal indicates that a trunk or circuit is busy. This is usually signaled with a fast busy tone.

name: LINEBUSYMODE_UNAVAIL
title: LINEBUSYMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBUSYMODE_UNAVAIL = 0x00000008 The busy signal's specific mode is unavailable and will not become known.

name: LINEBUSYMODE_UNKNOWN
title: LINEBUSYMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEBUSYMODE_UNKNOWN = 0x00000004 The busy signal's specific mode is currently unknown but may become known later.

name: LINECALLCOMPLCOND_BUSY
title: LINECALLCOMPLCOND (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLCOMPLCOND_BUSY = 0x00000001 Completion of the call under busy conditions.

name: LINECALLCOMPLCOND_NOANSWER
title: LINECALLCOMPLCOND (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLCOMPLCOND_NOANSWER = 0x00000002 Completion of the call under ringback no answer conditions.

name: LDAP_OPT_AREC_EXCLUSIVE
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_AREC_EXCLUSIVE (0x98) Performs an A-Record only DNS lookup on the supplied host string. This prevents false DNS queries from being generated when resolving host names. Use this flag whenever passing a host name as opposed to a domain name for the hostname parameter. This is a Microsoft-specific option. LDAP_OPT_ON or LDAP_OPT_OFF.

name: LDAP_OPT_AUTO_RECONNECT
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_AUTO_RECONNECT (0x91) Enables/disables auto-reconnect. A Microsoft-specific option.

name: LDAP_OPT_DEREF
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_DEREF (0x02) Determines how aliases are handled during search. LDAP_DEREF_NEVER (0x00) LDAP_DEREF_SEARCHING (0x01) LDAP_DEREF_FINDING (0x02) LDAP_DEREF_ALWAYS (0x03). The LDAP_DEREF_SEARCHING value means that aliases should be dereferenced during the search but not when locating the base object of the search. The LDAP_DEREF_FINDING value means that aliases should be dereferenced when locating the base object but not during the search.

name: LDAP_OPT_DESC
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_DESC (0x01) The underlying socket descriptor corresponding to the default LDAP connection. The value of the socket.

name: LDAP_OPT_DNSDOMAIN_NAME
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_DNSDOMAIN_NAME (0x3B) A Microsoft-specific option. The DNS host name.

name: LDAP_OPT_ERROR_NUMBER
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_ERROR_NUMBER (0x31) Provides an error code. This is a Microsoft-specific option. The code of the most recent LDAP error that occurred for this session.

name: LDAP_OPT_ERROR_STRING
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_ERROR_STRING (0x32) Provides an error message. This is a Microsoft-specific option. The message returned with the most recent LDAP error that occurred for this session.

name: LDAP_OPT_HOST_NAME
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_HOST_NAME (0x30) Specifies the default LDAP server. This is a Microsoft-specific option. The host name of the default LDAP server. Returns the host name of the server. The server-name string returned by this option should not be freed by the user because it is automatically freed when ldap_unbind is called

name: LDAP_OPT_HOST_REACHABLE
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_HOST_REACHABLE (0x3E) This is a Microsoft-specific option. LDAP_ON or LDAP_OFF.

name: LDAP_OPT_PROMPT_CREDENTIALS
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_PROMPT_CREDENTIALS (0x3F) Indicates whether to prompt for credentials. Currently needed only for distributed password authentication (DPA) and Windows® NT® LAN Manager if no credentials are loaded. A Microsoft-specific option.

name: LDAP_OPT_REFERRAL_HOP_LIMIT
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_REFERRAL_HOP_LIMIT ( 0x10) The number of referrals to allow. 0-0xFFFFFFFF. A value of LDAP_NO_LIMIT (zero) means that there is no limit. See also LDAP_OPT_REFERRALs.

name: LDAP_OPT_REFERRALS
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_REFERRALS (0x08) Controls whether the LDAP library automatically follows referrals returned by LDAP servers. LDAP_OPT_ON LDAP_OPT_OFF A value of LDAP_CHASE_SUBORDINATE_REFERRALS indicates that LDAP should chase subordinate referrals (or references) returned in a search (LDAP 3 or later). A value of LDAP_CHASE_EXTERNAL_REFERRALS indicates that LDAP should chase external referrals. These can be returned on any operation except a bind.

name: LDAP_OPT_RESTART
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_RESTART (0x09) Not supported Not supported.

name: LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_SERVER_ERROR (0x33) Provides an error message. This is a Microsoft-specific option The message returned with the most recent server error that occurred for this session.

name: LDAP_OPT_SIZELIMIT
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_SIZELIMIT (0x03) A limit on the number of entries to return from a search. 0-0xFFFFFFFF. A value of LDAP_NO_LIMIT (zero) means that there is no limit.

name: LDAP_OPT_SSL
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_SSL (0x0a) Enables Secure Socket Layer on connection. LDAP_OPT_ON or LDAP_OPT_OFF.

name: LDAP_OPT_SSPI_FLAGS
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_SSPI_FLAGS (0x92) Flags to pass to the SSPI function InitializeSecurityContext. A Microsoft-specific option.

name: LDAP_OPT_TIMELIMIT
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LDAP_OPT_TIMELIMIT (0x04) A limit on the number of seconds the server spends on a search. 0-0xFFFFFFFF. A value of LDAP_NO_LIMIT (zero) means that there is no limit.

name: LPDA_OPT_SERVER_EXT_ERROR
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LPDA_OPT_SERVER_EXT_ERROR (0x34) Provides a Win32 error code message. This is a Microsoft-specific option. The message returned with the most recent Win32 server error that occurred for this session.

name: PING_KEEP_ALIVE
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: PING_KEEP_ALIVE (0x36) The minimum number of seconds the run time waits, after the last response from the server, before sending a keep-alive ping. Default value is 120/5/maxInt seconds.

name: PING_LIMIT
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: PING_LIMIT (0x38) The number of unanswered pings that the run time sends before closing a connection. 4/0/maxInt.

name: PING_WAIT_TIME
title: Session Options (Windows CE 5.0)
row: PING_WAIT_TIME (0x37) The number of milliseconds that the run time waits for the response to come back after sending a ping. Default value is 2000/10/60000 milliseconds.

name: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_CALLBACK
title: LINECALLCOMPLMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_CALLBACK = 0x00000002 Requests the called station to return the call when it returns to idle.

name: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_CAMPON
title: LINECALLCOMPLMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_CAMPON = 0x00000001 Queues the call until the call can be completed.

name: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_INTRUDE
title: LINECALLCOMPLMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_INTRUDE = 0x00000004 Adds the application to the existing call at the called station (barge in).

name: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_MESSAGE
title: LINECALLCOMPLMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLCOMPLMODE_MESSAGE = 0x00000008 Leaves a short predefined message for the called station (Leave Word Calling). The message to be sent is specified separately.

name: LINECALLFEATURE_ACCEPT
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_ACCEPT = 0x000000001 Accept the call (lineAccept).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_ADDTOCONF
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_ADDTOCONF = 0x00000002 Add the call to the current conference (lineAddToConference).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_ANSWER
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_ANSWER = 0x00000004 Answer the call (lineAnswer).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_BLINDTRANSFER
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_BLINDTRANSFER = 0x00000008 Perform a blind transfer on the call (lineBlindTransfer).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_COMPLETETRANSF
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_COMPLETETRANSF = 0x00000020 Complete the call transfer (lineCompleteTransfer).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_DIAL
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_DIAL = 0x00000040 Dial the destination number for the call (lineDial).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_DROP
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_DROP = 0x00000080 Drop the call (lineDrop).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_GENERATEDIGITS
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_GENERATEDIGITS = 0x00000200 Generate digits on the call (lineGenerateDigits).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_GENERATETONE
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_GENERATETONE = 0x00000400 Generate tones on the call (lineGenerateTone).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_HOLD
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_HOLD = 0x00000800 Put the call on hold (lineHold).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_MONITORDIGITS
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_MONITORDIGITS = 0x00001000 Monitor digits on the call (lineMonitorDigits).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_MONITORMEDIA
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_MONITORMEDIA = 0x00002000 Monitor the call's media (lineMonitorMedia).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_PREPAREADDCONF
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_PREPAREADDCONF = 0x00010000 Prepare the call for addition to a conference (linePrepareAddToConference).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_REDIRECT
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_REDIRECT = 0x00020000 Redirect the call to another destination (lineRedirect).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_RELEASEUSERUSERINFO
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_RELEASEUSERUSERINFO = 0x10000000 Release current user-user information (lineReleaseUserUserInfo). (TAPI version 1.4 and later.)

name: LINECALLFEATURE_REMOVEFROMCONF
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_REMOVEFROMCONF = 0x00040000 Remove the call from the conference (lineRemoveFromConference).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SENDUSERUSER
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SENDUSERUSER = 0x00100000 Send user-user information (lineSendUserUserInfo).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SETCALLPARAMS
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SETCALLPARAMS = 0x00200000 Set call parameters (lineSetCallParams)

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SETQOS
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SETQOS = 0x40000000 Set QOS levels for the call. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SETTERMINAL
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SETTERMINAL = 0x00800000 Set the terminal to be used with the call (lineSetTerminal).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SETTREATMENT
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SETTREATMENT = 0x20000000 Set call treatment. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SETUPCONF
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SETUPCONF = 0x01000000 Set up a conference (lineSetupConference).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SETUPTRANSFER
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SETUPTRANSFER = 0x02000000 Set up a transfer (lineSetupTransfer).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_SWAPHOLD
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_SWAPHOLD = 0x04000000 Perform a swap hold operation (lineSwapHold).

name: LINECALLFEATURE_UNHOLD
title: LINECALLFEATURE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE_UNHOLD = 0x08000000 Take the call off hold (lineUnhold).

name: LINECALLFEATURE2_NOHOLDCONFERENCE
title: LINECALLFEATURE2 (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE2_NOHOLDCONFERENCE = 0x00000001 If this bit is on, a "no hold conference" can be created by using the LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_NOHOLDCONFERENCE option with lineSetupConference. The LINECALLFEATURE_SETUPCONF bit will also be on in the dwCallFeatures member in the LINECALLSTATUS structure.

name: LINECALLFEATURE2_ONESTEPTRANSFER
title: LINECALLFEATURE2 (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE2_ONESTEPTRANSFER = 0x00000002 If this bit is on, "one step transfer" can be created by using the LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_ONESTEPTRANSFER option with lineSetupTransfer. The LINECALLFEATURE_SETUPTRANSFER bit will also be on in the dwCallFeatures member.

name: LINECALLFEATURE2_TRANSFERCONF
title: LINECALLFEATURE2 (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLFEATURE2_TRANSFERCONF = 0x00000080 If this bit is on, the lineCompleteTransfer function can be used to resolve the transfer as a three-way conference. The LINECALLFEATURE_COMPLETETRANSF bit will also be on in the dwCallFeatures member.

name: LINECALLFEATURE2_TRANSFERNORM
title: LINECALLFEATURE2 (Windows CE 5.0)

row: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_DESTOFFHOOK = 0x00000010 The called party's phone should be automatically taken offhook.

name: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_IDLE
title: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_IDLE = 0x00000002 The call should be originated on an idle call appearance and not join a call in progress. When using the lineMakeCall function, if the LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_IDLE value is not set and there is an existing call on the line, the function breaks into the existing call if necessary to make the new call. If there is no existing call, the function makes the new call as specified.

name: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_NOHOLDCONFERENCE
title: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_NOHOLDCONFERENCE = 0x00000020 This bit is used only in conjunction with lineSetupConference and linePrepareAddToConference. The address to be conferenced with the current call is specified in the TargetAddress member in LINECALLPARAMS. The consultation call does not physically draw dial tone from the switch, but will progress through various call establishment states, for example, dialing and proceeding. When the consultation call reaches the connected state, the conference is automatically established. The original call, which had remained in the connected state, enters the conferenced state. The consultation call enters the conferenced state. The hConfCall parameter of linePrepareAddToConference enters the connected state. If the consultation call fails, enters the disconnected state followed by idle, the hConfCall also enters the idle state, and the original call, which may have been an existing conference, in the case of linePrepareAddToConference, remains in the connected state. The original party, or parties, never perceive the call has having gone onhold. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_ONESTEPTRANSFER
title: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_ONESTEPTRANSFER = 0x00000080 This bit is used only in conjunction with lineSetupTransfer. It combines the operation of lineSetupTransfer followed by lineDial on the consultation call into a single step. The address to be dialed is specified in the TargetAddress member in LINECALLPARAMS. The original call is placed in onholdpendingtransfer state, just as if lineSetupTransfer were called normally, and the consultation call is established normally. The application must still call lineCompleteTransfer to effect the transfer. This feature is often used when invoking a transfer from a server over a third-party call control link, because such links frequently do not support the normal two-step process. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_ORIGOFFHOOK
title: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_ORIGOFFHOOK = 0x00000008 The originator's phone should be automatically taken offhook.

name: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_PREDICTIVEDIAL
title: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_PREDICTIVEDIAL = 0x00000040 This bit is used only when placing a call on an address with predictive dialing capability (LINEADDRCAPFLAGS_PREDICTIVEDIALER is on in the dwAddrCapFlags member in LINEADDRESSCAPS). The bit must be on to enable the enhanced call progress and or the media device monitoring capabilities of the device. If this bit is not on, the call will be placed without enhanced call progress or media type monitoring, and no automatic transfer will be initiated based on call state. TAPI version 2.0 and later.

name: LINECALLREASON_ROUTEREQUEST
title: LINECALLREASON (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLREASON_ROUTEREQUEST = 0x00008000 The call appears on the address because the switch needs routing instructions from the application. The application should examine the CalledID member in LINECALLINFO, and use the lineRedirect function to provide a new dialable address for the call. name: LINECALLSTATE_ACCEPTED
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_ACCEPTED = 0x00000004 The call was in the offering state and has been accepted. This indicates to other, monitoring, applications that the current owner application has claimed responsibility for answering the call. In ISDN, the accepted state is entered when the called-party equipment sends a message to the switch indicating that it is willing to present the call to the called person. This has the side effect of alerting (ringing) the users at both ends of the call. An incoming call can always be immediately answered without first being separately accepted.

name: LINECALLSTATE_BUSY
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_BUSY = 0x00000040 The call is receiving a busy tone. A busy tone indicates that the call cannot be completed. This occurs if either a circuit (trunk) or the remote party's station are in use.

name: LINECALLSTATE_CONFERENCED
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_CONFERENCED = 0x00000800 The call is a member of a conference call and is logically in the connected state.

name: LINECALLSTATE_CONNECTED
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_CONNECTED = 0x00000100 The call has been established and the connection is made. Information is able to flow over the call between the originating address and the destination address.

name: LINECALLSTATE_DIALING
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_DIALING = 0x0000010 The originator is dialing digits on the call. The dialed digits are collected by the switch. Note that neither lineGenerateDigits nor TSPI_lineGenerateDigits will place the line into the dialing state.

name: LINECALLSTATE_DIALTONE
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_DIALTONE = 0x00000008 The call is receiving a dial tone from the switch. This means that the switch is ready to receive a dialed number.

name: LINECALLSTATE_DISCONNECTED
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_DISCONNECTED = 0x00004000 The remote party has disconnected from the call.

name: LINECALLSTATE_IDLE
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_IDLE = 0x00000001 The call exists but has not been connected. No activity exists on the call. This means that no call is currently active. A call can never transition out of the idle state.

name: LINECALLSTATE_OFFERING
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_OFFERING = 0x000000002 The call is being offered to the station, signaling the arrival of a new call. The offering state is not the same as causing a phone or computer to ring. In some environments, a call in the offering state does not ring the user until the switch instructs the line to ring. For example this state is in use when an incoming call appears on several station sets but only the primary address rings. The instruction to ring does not affect any call states.

name: LINECALLSTATE_ONHOLD
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_ONHOLD = 0x00000400 The call is on hold by the switch. This frees the physical line. This allows another call to use the line.

name: LINECALLSTATE_ONHOLDPENDCONF
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_ONHOLDPENDCONF = 0x00001000 The call is currently on hold while it is being added to a conference.

name: LINECALLSTATE_ONHOLDPENDTRANSFER
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_ONHOLDPENDTRANSFER = 0x00002000 The call is currently on hold awaiting transfer to another number.

name: LINECALLSTATE_PROCEEDING
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_PROCEEDING = 0x00000200 Dialing has completed and the call is proceeding through the switch or telephone network. This occurs after dialing is complete and before the call reaches the dialed party, as indicated by ringback, busy, or answer.

name: LINECALLSTATE_RINGBACK
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_RINGBACK = 0x00000020 The station to be called has been reached, and the destination's switch is generating a ring tone back to the originator. A ringback means that the destination address is being alerted to the call.

name: LINECALLSTATE_SPECIALINFO
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_SPECIALINFO = 0x00000080 The call is receiving a special information signal that precedes a prerecorded announcement indicating why a call cannot be completed.

name: LINECALLSTATE_UNKNOWN
title: LINECALLSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLSTATE_UNKNOWN = 0x00008000 The call exists, but its state is currently unknown. This may be the result of poor call progress detection by the service provider. A call state message with the call state set to unknown may also be generated to inform the TAPI DLL about a new call at a time when the actual call state of the call is not exactly known

name: LINECALLTREATMENT_BUSY
title: LINECALLTREATMENT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLTREATMENT_BUSY = 0x00000003 When the call is not actively connected to a device, offering or onhold, the party hears busy signal.

name: LINECALLTREATMENT_MUSIC
title: LINECALLTREATMENT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLTREATMENT_MUSIC = 0x00000004 When the call is not actively connected to a device, offering or onhold, the party hears music.

name: LINECALLTREATMENT_RINGBACK
title: LINECALLTREATMENT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLTREATMENT_RINGBACK = 0x00000002 When the call is not actively connected to a device, offering or onhold, the party hears ringback tone.

name: LINECALLTREATMENT_SILENCE
title: LINECALLTREATMENT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECALLTREATMENT_SILENCE = 0x00000001 When the call is not actively connected to a device, offering or onhold, the party hears silence.

name: LINECONNECTEDMODE_ACTIVE
title: LINECONNECTEDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECONNECTEDMODE_ACTIVE = 0x00000001 Indicates that the call is connected at the current station (the current station is a participant in the call). If the call state mode is zero (0), the application should assume that the value is "active" This would be the situation on a non-bridged address. The mode can switch between ACTIVE and INACTIVE during a call if the user joins and leaves the call through manual action. In such a bridged situation, a lineDrop or lineHold function call may possibly not actually drop the call or place it on hold, because the status of other stations on the call may govern. For example, attempting to "hold" a call when other stations are participating won't be possible. Instead, the call may simply be changed to the INACTIVE mode if it remains CONNECTED at other stations.

name: LINECONNECTEDMODE_ACTIVEHELD
title: LINECONNECTEDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECONNECTEDMODE_ACTIVEHELD = 0x00000004 Indicates that the station is an active participant in the call, but that the remote party has placed the call on hold. The other party considers the call to be in the onhold state. Normally, such information is available only when both endpoints of the call fall within the same switching domain. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 2.0 or higher. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINECONNECTEDMODE_CONFIRMED
title: LINECONNECTEDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECONNECTEDMODE_CONFIRMED = 0x00000010 Indicates that the service provider received affirmative notification that the call has entered the connected state. For example, the notification was received through answer supervision or similar mechanisms. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 2.0 or higher. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINECONNECTEDMODE_INACTIVE
title: LINECONNECTEDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECONNECTEDMODE_INACTIVE = 0x00000002 Indicates that the call is active at one or more other stations, but the current station is not a participant in the call. If the call state mode is ZERO, the application should assume that the value is "active". This would be the situation on a non-bridged address. A call in the INACTIVE state can be joined using lineAnswer. Many operations that are valid in calls in the CONNECTED state can be impossible in the INACTIVE mode, such as monitoring for tones and digits, because the station is not actually participating in the call; monitoring is usually suspended, although not canceled, while the call is in the INACTIVE mode.

name: LINECONNECTEDMODE_INACTIVEHELD
title: LINECONNECTEDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINECONNECTEDMODE_INACTIVEHELD = 0x00000008 Indicates that the station is not an active participant in the call, and that the remote party has placed the call on hold. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 2.0 or higher. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CALLHUB
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CALLHUB = 0x00000400 Indicates whether call hubs are supported on this line. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 3.0 or higher.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CALLHUBTRACKING
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CALLHUBTRACKING = 0x00000800 Indicates whether call hub tracking is supported on this line. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 3.0 or higher.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CLOSEDROP
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CLOSEDROP = 0x00000020 Specifies what happens when an open line is closed while the application has calls active on the line. If TRUE, the service provider drops, clears, all active calls on the line when the last application that has opened the line closes it with lineClose. If FALSE, the service provider does not drop active calls in such cases. Instead, the calls remain active and under control of external devices. A service provider typically sets this bit to FALSE if there is some other device that can keep the call alive, for example, if an analog line has the computer and phone set both connect directly to them in a party-line configuration, the offhook phone will automatically keep the call active even after the computer powers down. Applications should check this flag to determine whether to warn the user, with an OK/Cancel dialog box, that active calls will be lost.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CROSSADDRCONF
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_CROSSADDRCONF = 0x00000001 Specifies whether calls on different addresses on this line can be conferenced.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_HIGHLEVCOMP
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_HIGHLEVCOMP = 0x00000002 Specifies whether high-level compatibility information elements are supported on this line.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_LOWLEVCOMP
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_LOWLEVCOMP = 0x00000004 Specifies whether low-level compatibility information elements are supported on this line.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_MEDIACONTROL
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_MEDIACONTROL = 0x00000008 Specifies whether media-control operations are available for calls at this line.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_MSP
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_MSP = 0x00000200 Indicates whether a Media Service Provider (MSP) is associated with the line. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 3.0 or higher.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_MULTIPLEADDR
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_MULTIPLEADDR = 0x00000010 Specifies whether lineMakeCall, lineDial, TSPI_lineMakeCall, or TSPI_lineDial is able to deal with multiple addresses at once, as they are for inverse multiplexing.

name: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_PRIVATEOBJECTS
title: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVCAPFLAGS_PRIVATEOBJECTS = 0x00001000 Indicates whether provider-specific Interfaces have been implemented. This flag is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 3.0 or higher.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_BATTERY
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_BATTERY = 0x00008000 The battery level has changed significantly. This condition applies to cellular phones.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_CAPSCHANGE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_CAPSCHANGE = 0x00100000 Indicates that, due to configuration changes made by the user or by other circumstances, one or more of the members in the LINEDEVCAPS structure for the address have changed. The application should use lineGetDevCaps to read the updated structure. If a service provider sends a LINE_LINEDEVSTATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later. Applications negotiating a previous TAPI version will receive LINE_LINEDEVSTATE messages specifying LINEDEVSTATE_REINIT, requiring them to shut down and reinitialize their connection to TAPI to obtain the updated information.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_CLOSE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_CLOSE = 0x00000400 The line has been closed by another application.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_CONFIGCHANGE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_CONFIGCHANGE = 0x00200000 Indicates that configuration changes have been made to one or more of the media devices associated with the line device. The application, if it desires, can use lineGetDevConfig to read the updated information. If a service provider sends a LINE_LINEDEVSTATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later. Applications negotiating a previous API version will not receive any notification.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_CONNECTED
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_CONNECTED = 0x00000004 The line was previously disconnected and is now connected to TAPI.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_DEVSPECIFIC
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_DEVSPECIFIC = 0x00020000 The line's device-specific information has changed.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_DISCONNECTED
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_DISCONNECTED = 0x00000008 This line was previously connected and is now disconnected from TAPI.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_INSERVICE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_INSERVICE = 0x00000040 The line is connected to TAPI. This happens when TAPI is first activated or when the line wire is physically plugged in and in-service at the switch while TAPI is active.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_LOCK
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_LOCK = 0x00080000 The locked status of the line device has changed.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_MAINTENANCE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_MAINTENANCE = 0x00000100 Maintenance is being performed on the line at the switch. TAPI cannot be used to operate on the line device.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_MSGWAITOFF
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_MSGWAITOFF = 0x00000020 The message waiting indicator is turned off.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_MSGWAITON
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_MSGWAITON = 0x00000010 The message waiting indicator is turned on.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_NUMCALLS
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_NUMCALLS = 0x00000800 The number of calls on the line device has changed.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_NUMCOMPLETIONS
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_NUMCOMPLETIONS = 0x00001000 The number of outstanding call completions on the line device has changed.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_OPEN
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_OPEN = 0x00000200 The line has been opened by another application.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_OTHER
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_OTHER = 0x00000001 Device-status items other than those listed below have changed. The application should check the current device status to determine which items have changed.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_OUTOFSERVICE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_OUTOFSERVICE = 0x00000080 The line is out of service at the switch or physically disconnected. TAPI cannot be used to operate on the line device.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_REINIT
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_REINIT = 0x00040000 Items have changed in the configuration of line devices. To become aware of these changes, for example to become aware ofthe appearance of new line devices, the application should reinitialize its use of TAPI.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_REMOVED
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_REMOVED = 0x01000000 Indicates that the device is being removed from the system by the service provider most likely through user action, through a control panel or similar utility. A LINE_LINEDEVSTATE message with this value will normally be immediately followed by a LINE_CLOSE message on the device. Subsequent attempts to access the device prior to TAPI being reinitialized will result in LINEERR_NODEVICE being returned to the application. If a service provider sends a LINE_LINEDEVSTATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later. Applications negotiating a previous API version will not receive any notification.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_RINGING
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_RINGING = 0x00000002 The switch tells the line to alert the user. TAPI: Service providers notify applications on each ring cycle by repeatedly sending LINE_LINEDEVSTATE messages containing this constant. For example, in the United States, service providers send a message with this constant every six seconds. TSPI: On a POTS device, the service provider can send the message whenever the central office sends ring voltage. On digital devices such as ISDN, the service provider may need to synthesize the repetition of the message if the switch generates only one ring request. Each repetition of the message should show the ring count increasing, so that toll save functions work properly.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_ROAMMODE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_ROAMMODE = 0x00004000 The roam mode of the line device has changed.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_SIGNAL
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_SIGNAL = 0x00010000 The signal level has changed significantly (cellular).

name: LINEDEVSTATE_TERMINALS
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_TERMINALS = 0x00002000 The terminal settings have changed. This can happen, for example, if multiple line devices share terminals among them. For example, this can happen when two lines share a phone terminal.

name: LINEDEVSTATE_TRANSLATECHANGE
title: LINEDEVSTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATE_TRANSLATECHANGE = 0x00400000 Indicates that, due to configuration changes made by the user or other circumstances, one or more of the members in the LINETRANSLATECAPS structure have changed. The application should use lineGetTranslateCaps to read the updated structure. If a service provider sends a LINE_LINEDEVSTATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later. Applications negotiating a previous TAPI version will receive LINE_LINEDEVSTATE messages specifying LINEDEVSTATE_REINIT, requiring them to shut down and reinitialize their connection to TAPI to obtain the updated information.

name: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS_INSERVICE
title: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS_INSERVICE = 0x00000004 Indicates whether the line is in service. If TRUE, the line is in service. If FALSE, the line is out of service.

name: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS_LOCKED
title: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS_LOCKED = 0x00000008 Indicates whether the line is locked or unlocked. This bit is most often used with line devices associated with cellular phones. Many cellular phones have a security mechanism that requires the entry of a password to enable the phone to place calls. This bit can be used to indicate to applications that the phone is locked and cannot place calls until the password is entered on the user interface of the phone so that the application can present an appropriate alert to the user.

name: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS_MSGWAIT
title: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDEVSTATUSFLAGS_MSGWAIT = 0x00000002 Indicates whether the line has a message waiting. If TRUE, a message is waiting. If FALSE, no message is waiting.

name: LINEDIALTONEMODE_EXTERNAL
title: LINEDIALTONEMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIALTONEMODE_EXTERNAL = 0x00000008 This is an external (public network) dial tone.

name: LINEDIALTONEMODE_INTERNAL
title: LINEDIALTONEMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIALTONEMODE_INTERNAL = 0x00000004 This is an internal dial tone, as within a PBX.

name: LINEDIALTONEMODE_NORMAL
title: LINEDIALTONEMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIALTONEMODE_NORMAL = 0x00000001 This is a normal dial tone, which typically is a continuous tone.

name: LINEDIALTONEMODE_SPECIAL
title: LINEDIALTONEMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIALTONEMODE_SPECIAL = 0x00000002 This is a special dial tone indicating that a certain condition, known by the switch or network, is currently in effect. Special dial tones typically use an interrupted tone. As with a normal dial tone, this indicates that the switch is ready to receive the number to be dialed.

name: LINEDIALTONEMODE_UNAVAIL
title: LINEDIALTONEMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIALTONEMODE_UNAVAIL = 0x00000020 The dial tone mode is unavailable and will not become known.

name: LINEDIALTONEMODE_UNKNOWN
title: LINEDIALTONEMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIALTONEMODE_UNKNOWN = 0x00000010 The dial tone mode is not currently known but may become known later.

name: LINEDIGITMODE_DTMF
title: LINEDIGITMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIGITMODE_DTMF = 0x00000002 Uses DTMF tones to signal digits. Valid digits are zero (0) through 9, '*', '#', 'A', 'B', 'C', and 'D'.

name: LINEDIGITMODE_DTMFEND
title: LINEDIGITMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIGITMODE_DTMFEND = 0x00000004 Uses DTMF tones to signal digits and detect the down edges. Valid digits are zero (0) through 9, '*', '#', 'A', 'B', 'C', and 'D'.

name: LINEDIGITMODE_PULSE
title: LINEDIGITMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDIGITMODE_PULSE = 0x00000001 Uses rotary pulse sequences to signal digits. Valid digits are zero (0) through 9.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BADADDRESS
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BADADDRESS = 0x00000080 The destination address is invalid.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BLOCKED
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BLOCKED = 0x00020000 The call could not be connected because calls from the origination address are not being accepted at the destination address. This differs from LINEDISCONNECTMODE_REJECT in that blocking is implemented in the network (a passive reject) while a rejection is implemented in the destination equipment (an active reject). The blocking can be due to a specific exclusion of the origination address, or because the destination accepts calls from only a selected set of origination address (closed user group). TAPI versions 2.0 and later. LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BLOCKED is appropriate as a blacklisted response. For example, a modem has received an answer, gone more than six seconds without detecting Ringback, failed to connect a defined number of times, determines that the phone number is not valid to call, and issues a 'blacklisted' response.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BUSY
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_BUSY = 0x00000020 The remote user's station is busy.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_CANCELLED
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_CANCELLED = 0x00080000 The call was cancelled. (TAPI versions 2.0 and later.)

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_CONGESTION
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_CONGESTION = 0x00000200 The network is congested.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_DONOTDISTURB
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_DONOTDISTURB = 0x00040000 The call could not be connected because the destination has invoked the Do Not Disturb feature. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_FORWARDED
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_FORWARDED = 0x00000010 The call was forwarded by the switch.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_INCOMPATIBLE
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_INCOMPATIBLE = 0x00000400 The remote user's station equipment is incompatible with the type of call requested.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NOANSWER
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NOANSWER = 0x00000040 The remote user's station does not answer.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NODIALTONE
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NODIALTONE = 0x00001000 A dial tone was not detected within a service-provider defined timeout, at a point during dialing when one was expected (such as at a "W" in the dialable string). This can also occur without a service-provider-defined timeout period or without a value specified in the dwWaitForDialTone member of the LINEDIALPARAMS structure. TAPI versions 1.4 and later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NORMAL
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NORMAL = 0x00000001 This is a normal disconnect request by the remote party. The call was terminated normally.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NUMBERCHANGED
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_NUMBERCHANGED = 0x00002000 The call could not be connected because the destination number has been changed, but automatic redirection to the new number is not provided. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_OUTOFORDER
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_OUTOFORDER = 0x00004000 The call could not be connected or was disconnected because the destination device is out of order. This could occur if for example there were hardware failure. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_PICKUP
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_PICKUP = 0x00000008 The call was picked up from elsewhere.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_QOSUNAVAIL
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_QOSUNAVAIL = 0x00010000 The call could not be connected or was disconnected because the minimum quality of service could not be obtained or sustained. This differs from LINEDISCONNECTMODE_INCOMPATIBLE in that the lack of resources may be a temporary condition at the destination. TAPI versions 2.0 and later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_REJECT
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_REJECT = 0x00000004 The remote user has rejected the call.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_TEMPFAILURE
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_TEMPFAILURE = 0x00008000 The call could not be connected or was disconnected because of a temporary failure in the network; the call can be reattempted later and is expected to eventually complete. TAPI versions 2.0 and later. LINEDISCONNECTMODE_TEMPFAILURE is appropriate as a delayed response. For example, a modem getting a busy signal or equivalent too many times in a particular time period concludes that the number should not be called again until a defined time has elapsed and issues a 'delayed' response.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_UNAVAIL
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_UNAVAIL = 0x00000800 The reason for the disconnect is unavailable and will not become known later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_UNKNOWN
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_UNKNOWN = 0x00000002 The reason for the disconnect request is unknown but may become known later.

name: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_UNREACHABLE
title: LINEDISCONNECTMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEDISCONNECTMODE_UNREACHABLE = 0x00000100 The remote user could not be reached.

name: LINEERR_ADDRESSBLOCKED

name: LINEERR_ALLOCATED

name: LINEERR_BADDEVICEID

name: LINEERR_BEARERMODEUNAVAIL

row: LINEERR_BEARERMODEUNAVAIL = 0x00000003 The bearer mode member in LINECALLPARAMS is invalid, the bearer mode specified in LINECALLPARAMS is not available, or the call's bearer mode cannot be changed to the specified bearer mode.

name: LINEERR_BILLINGREJECTED
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_BILLINGREJECTED = 0x80000054 The billing mode of the call was rejected.

name: LINEERR_CALLUNAVAIL
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_CALLUNAVAIL = 0x0000005 All call appearances on the specified address are currently in use.

name: LINEERR_COMPLETIONOVERRUN

row: LINEERR_COMPLETIONOVERRUN = 0x0000006 The maximum number of outstanding call completions has been exceeded.

name: LINEERR_CONFERENCEFULL
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_CONFERENCEFULL = 0x00000007 The maximum number of parties for a conference has been reached, or the requested number of parties cannot be satisfied.

name: LINEERR_DIALBILLING
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_DIALBILLING = 0x00000008 The dialable address parameter contains dialing control characters that are not processed by the service provider.

name: LINEERR_DIALDIALTONE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_DIALDIALTONE = 0x00000009 The dialable address parameter contains dialing control characters that are not processed by the service provider.

name: LINEERR_DIALPROMPT
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_DIALPROMPT = 0x8000000A The dialable address parameter contains dialing control characters that are not processed by the service provider.

name: LINEERR_DIALQUIET
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_DIALQUIET = 0x8000000B The dialable address parameter contains dialing control characters that are not processed by the service provider.

name: LINEERR_DIALVOICEDETECT
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_DIALVOICEDETECT = 0x8000005C Use of the ":" dial modifier is not supported. This value is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 2.0 or higher.

name: LINEERR_INCOMPATIBLEAPIVERSION
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INCOMPATIBLEAPIVERSION = 0x8000000C The application requested a TAPI version or version range that is either incompatible with, or cannot be supported by, the Telephony API implementation and the corresponding service provider.

name: LINEERR_INCOMPATIBLEEXTVERSION
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INCOMPATIBLEEXTVERSION = 0x8000000D The application requested an extension version range that is either invalid or cannot be supported by the corresponding service provider.

name: LINEERR_INIFILECORRUPT
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INIFILECORRUPT = 0x8000000E The Telephon.ini file cannot be read or understood properly by TAPI because of internal inconsistencies or formatting problems. For example, the [Locations], [Cards], or [Countries] section of the Telephon.ini file may be corrupted or inconsistent.

name: LINEERR_INUSE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INUSE = 0x8000000F The line device is in use and cannot currently be configured, allow a party to be added, allow a call to be answered, allow a call to be placed, or allow a call to be transferred.

name: LINEERR_INVALADDRESS
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALADDRESS = 0x80000010 A specified address is either invalid or not allowed. If invalid, the address contains invalid characters or digits, or the destination address contains dialing control characters, W, @, $, or ?, that are not supported by the service provider. If the address is not allowed, the specified address is either not assigned to the specified line or is not valid for address redirection.

name: LINEERR_INVALADDRESSID
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALADDRESSID = 0x80000011 The specified address identifier is either invalid or out of range.

name: LINEERR_INVALADDRESSMODE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALADDRESSMODE = 0x80000012 The specified address mode is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALADDRESSSTATE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALADDRESSSTATE = 0x80000013 The specified address state contains one or more bits that are not LINEADDRESSSTATE.

name: LINEERR_INVALAPPHANDLE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALAPPHANDLE = 0x80000014 The application handle (such as specified by a hLineApp parameter) or the application registration handle is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALAPPNAME
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALAPPNAME = 0x80000015 The specified application name is invalid. If an application name is specified by the application, it is assumed that the string does not contain any non-displayable characters, and is zero-terminated.

name: LINEERR_INVALBEARERMODE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALBEARERMODE = 0x80000016 The specified bearer mode is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCALLHANDLE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCALLHANDLE = 0x80000018 The specified call handle is not valid. For example, the handle is not NULL but does not belong to the given line. In some cases, the specified call device handle is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCALLPARAMS
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCALLPARAMS = 0x80000019 The specified call parameters are invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCALLPRIVILEGE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCALLPRIVILEGE = 0x8000001A The specified call privilege parameter is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCALLSELECT
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCALLSELECT = 0x8000001B The specified select parameter is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCALLSTATE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCALLSTATE = 0x8000001C The current state of a call is not in a valid state for the requested operation.

name: LINEERR_INVALCALLSTATELIST
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)

name: LINEERR_INVALCARD
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)

name: LINEERR_INVALCOMPLETIONID
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCOMPLETIONID = 0x8000001F The completion identifier is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCONFCALLHANDLE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCONFCALLHANDLE = 0x80000020 The specified call handle for the conference call is invalid or is not a handle for a conference call.

name: LINEERR_INVALCONSULTCALLHANDLE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCONSULTCALLHANDLE = 0x80000021 The specified consultation call handle is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALCOUNTRYCODE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALCOUNTRYCODE = 0x80000022 The specified country/region code is invalid.

name: LINEERR_INVALDEVICECLASS
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALDEVICECLASS = 0x80000023 The line device has no associated device for the given device class, or the specified line does not support the indicated device class.

name: LINEERR_INVALDEVICEHANDLE
title: LINEERR (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEERR_INVALDEVICEHANDLE = 0x80000024 The line device handle is invalid.

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSY

row: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSY = 0x00000010 Forward all calls on busy, regardless of their origin. Use this value when forwarding for internal and external calls on busy and on no answer cannot be controlled separately.

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSYEXTERNAL
title: LINEFORWARDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSYEXTERNAL = 0x00000040 Forward all external calls on busy. Use this value when forwarding for internal and external calls on busy and on no answer can be controlled separately.

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSYINTERNAL
title: LINEFORWARDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSYINTERNAL = 0x00000020 Forward all internal calls on busy. Use this value when forwarding for internal and external calls on busy and on no answer can be controlled separately.

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSYNA
title: LINEFORWARDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEFORWARDMODE_BUSYNA = 0x00001000 Forward all calls on busy/no answer, regardless of their origin. Use this value when forwarding for internal and external calls on busy and on no answer cannot be controlled separately.

row: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNCOND = 0x00000001 Forward all calls unconditionally, regardless of their origin. Use this value when unconditional forwarding for internal and external calls cannot be controlled separately. Unconditional forwarding overrides forwarding on busy and/or no answer conditions.

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNCONDEXTERNAL

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNCONDINTERNAL

row: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNCONDINTERNAL = 0x00000002 Forward all internal calls unconditionally. Use this value when unconditional forwarding for internal and external calls can be controlled separately.

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNCONDSPECIFIC

row: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNCONDSPECIFIC = 0x00000008 Unconditionally forward all calls that originated at a specified address (selective call forwarding).

name: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNKNOWN
title: LINEFORWARDMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEFORWARDMODE_UNKNOWN = 0x00010000 Calls are forwarded, but the conditions under which forwarding will occur are not known at this time. It is possible that the conditions may become known at a future time. TAPI versions 1.4 and later.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_ADSI
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_ADSI = 0x00002000 An Analog Display Services Interface (ADSI) session on the call. ADSI enhances voice calls with alphanumeric information downloaded to the phone and the use of soft buttons on the phone.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_AUTOMATEDVOICE
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_AUTOMATEDVOICE = 0x00000008 Voice energy was detected on the call, and the voice is locally handled by an automated application such as with an answering machine application. When a service provider cannot distinguish between interactive and automated voice on an incoming call, it will report the call as interactive voice.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_DATAMODEM
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_DATAMODEM = 0x00000010 A data modem session on the call. Current modem protocols require the called station to initiate the handshake. For an incoming data modem call, the application can typically make no positive detection. How the service provider makes this determination is its choice. For example, a period of silence just after answering an incoming call can be used as a heuristic to decide that this might be a data modem call.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_DIGITALDATA
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_DIGITALDATA = 0x00000100 A digital data stream of unspecified format.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_G3FAX
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_G3FAX = 0x00000020 A group 3 fax is being sent or received over the call.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_G4FAX
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_G4FAX = 0x00000080 A group 4 fax is being sent or received over the call.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_INTERACTIVEVOICE
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_INTERACTIVEVOICE = 0x00000004 Voice energy was detected on the call, and the call is handled as an interactive voice call with humans on both ends.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_MIXED
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_MIXED = 0x00001000 A mixed session on the call. Mixed is one of the ISDN telematic services.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_TDD
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_TDD = 0x00000040 A Telephony Devices for the Deaf (TDD) () session on the call.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_TELETEX
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_TELETEX = 0x00000200 A teletex session on the call. Teletex is one of the telematic services.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_TELEX
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_TELEX = 0x00000800 A telex session on the call. Telex is one of the telematic services.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_UNKNOWN
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_UNKNOWN = 0x00000002 A media stream exists but its mode is not currently known and may become known later. This would correspond to a call with an unclassified media type. In typical analog telephony environments, an incoming call's media type may be unknown until after the call has been answered and the media stream has been filtered to make a determination. If the unknown media-mode flag is set, other media flags can also be set. This is used to signify that the media is unknown but that it is likely to be one of the other selected media types.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_VIDEOTEX
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_VIDEOTEX = 0x00000400 A videotex session on the call. Videotex is one the telematic services.

name: LINEMEDIAMODE_VOICEVIEW
title: LINEMEDIAMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEMEDIAMODE_VOICEVIEW = 0x00004000 The media type of the call is VoiceView. TAPI versions 1.4 and later.

name: LINEOFFERINGMODE_ACTIVE
title: LINEOFFERINGMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEOFFERINGMODE_ACTIVE = 0x00000001 Indicates that the call is alerting at the current station and if any application is set up to automatically answer, it can do so. If the call state mode is ZERO, the application should assume that the value is active. This would be the situation on a non-bridged address. TAPI versions 1.4 and later.

name: LINEOFFERINGMODE_INACTIVE
title: LINEOFFERINGMODE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINEOFFERINGMODE_INACTIVE = 0x00000002 Indicates that the call is being offered at more than one station, but the current station is not alerting. For example, it may be an attendant station where the offering status is advisory, such as blinking a light. Software at the station set for automatic answering should preferably not answer the call, because this should be the prerogative at the primary (alerting) station, but lineAnswer may be used to connect the call. TAPI versions 1.4 and later.

This is commonly used by data modem and fax applications to prevent interruption of calls by call waiting beeps. If no Cancel Call Waiting string is defined for the location, this bit has no affect. Note that applications using this bit are advised to also set the LINECALLPARAMFLAGS_SECURE bit in the dwCallParamFlags member of the LINECALLPARAMS structure passed in to lineMakeCall through the lpCallParams parameter, so that if the line device uses a mechanism other than dialable digits to suppress call interrupts that that mechanism will be invoked. title: LINETRANSLATERESULT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINETRANSLATERESULT_LONGDISTANCE = 0x00000004 Indicates that the call is being treated as a long distance call. Country/region code specified in the destination address is the same but area code is different from those specified for the CurrentLocation.

name: LINETRANSLATERESULT_NOTINTOLLLIST
title: LINETRANSLATERESULT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINETRANSLATERESULT_NOTINTOLLLIST = 0x00000020 Indicates that the country/region supports toll calling but the prefix does not appear in the TollPrefixList, so the call is dialed as a local call. Note that if both INTOLLIST and NOTINTOLLIST are off, the current country/region does not support toll prefixes, and user-interface elements related to toll prefixes should not be presented to the user. If either such bit is on, the country/region does support toll lists, and the related user-interface elements should be enabled.

name: LINETRANSLATERESULT_VOICEDETECT
title: LINETRANSLATERESULT (Windows CE 5.0)
row: LINETRANSLATERESULT_VOICEDETECT = 0x00000400 Indicates that the returned dialable address contains a ":". This element is exposed only to applications that negotiate a TAPI version of 2.0 or higher. Note The ":" (colon) character will be added to the list of characters that can be embedded in a dialable string and passed into destination addresses. Attempting to pass it from an application to a line device that supports an API version earlier than 2.0 will most likely result in LINEERR_INVALADDRESS, or possibly in the character being ignored entirely. The meaning of this character is "Pause until a voice prompt is detected, then continue dialing"; it is intended for use when automatically dialing into systems that give voice prompts, such as long distance calling card processors.

name: PHONEPRIVILEGE_MONITOR

row: PHONEPRIVILEGE_MONITOR = 0x00000001 An application that opens a phone device with the monitor privilege is informed about events and state changes occurring on the phone. The application cannot invoke any operations on the phone device that would change its state. Therefore only status operations can be invoked. Multiple applications can monitor a phone device at any given time.

name: PHONEPRIVILEGE_OWNER
title: PHONEPRIVILEGE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: PHONEPRIVILEGE_OWNER = 0x00000002 An application that opens a phone device with the owner privilege is allowed to change the state of the lamps, ringer, display, hookswitch, and data blocks of the phone. Opening a phone device in owner mode also provides monitoring of the phone device. Only one application is allowed to be the owner of a phone device at any given time.

name: PHONESTATE_CAPSCHANGE
title: PHONESTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: PHONESTATE_CAPSCHANGE = 0x00400000 Indicates that, due to configuration changes made by the user or other circumstances, one or more of the members in the PHONECAPS structure have changed. The application should use phoneGetDevCaps to read the updated structure. If a service provider sends a PHONE_STATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later; applications negotiating a previous API version will receive PHONE_STATE messages specifying PHONESTATE_REINIT, requiring them to shut down and reinitialize their connection to TAPI to obtain the updated information.

name: PHONESTATE_REMOVED
title: PHONESTATE (Windows CE 5.0)
row: PHONESTATE_REMOVED = 0x00800000 Indicates that the device is being removed from the system by the service provider, most likely through user action, through a control panel, or through a similar utility. A PHONE_STATE message with this value will normally be immediately followed by a PHONE_CLOSE message on the device. Subsequent attempts to access the device prior to TAPI being reinitialized will result in PHONEERR_NODEVICE being returned to the application. If a service provider sends a PHONE_STATE message containing this value to TAPI, TAPI will pass it along to applications that have negotiated TAPI version 1.4 or later. Applications negotiating a previous API version will not receive any notification.

name: HTTP_STATUS_RETRY_WITH

name: HTTP_STATUS_SERVICE_UNAVAIL

name: HTTP_STATUS_SWITCH_PROTOCOLS

name: HTTP_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA

name: HTTP_STATUS_URI_TOO_LONG

name: HTTP_STATUS_USE_PROXY
